record.context_brief: Flow-level control for measure differential equations
record.original_question: For measure differential equations on a manifold, where the non-variational setting uses probability vector fields that have only an abelian monoid structure rather than a Lie algebra structure, can one develop a mathematically useful control theory at the level of the induced flows instead of at the level of solutions, by leveraging geometric control techniques?

evidence.quote: On the other side, if one wants to use a non-variational interpretation, then the setting of MDEs suffers from the fact that PVFs enjoy only a structure of abelian monoid and not of Lie algebra. A possibility is to explore control properties at the level of the flows, instead of solutions, taking advantage of the geometric control techniques [3].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and let $\mathcal{P}(M)$ denote the space of Borel probability measures on $M$. A probability vector field (PVF) on $M$ is a Borel map $V:\mathcal{P}(M)\to \mathcal{P}(TM)$ such that for every $\mu\in\mathcal{P}(M)$ the pushforward of $V(\mu)$ by the canonical projection $\pi:TM\to M$ equals $\mu$. A measure differential equation (MDE) driven by a PVF $V$ is the evolution problem of finding a continuous curve $t\mapsto \mu_t\in\mathcal{P}(M)$ satisfying, in the sense of distributions,
$$\partial_t \mu_t + \mathrm{div}_x\!\big(\,\textstyle\int_{T_x M} v\, dV(\mu_t)(x,v)\,\big) = 0,$$
or more generally the generalized notion of solution in which $\mu_t$ is obtained as a limit of Euler-type discrete schemes built from $V$. Under composition of the associated time-$t$ flows on $\mathcal{P}(M)$, the family of PVFs carries only the algebraic structure of an abelian monoid (with composition of induced flows as the operation), and does not in general carry a Lie algebra structure analogous to the one available for smooth vector fields on $M$.

A controlled MDE is the data of a family $\{V_u\}_{u\in U}$ of PVFs parameterized by a control set $U$, together with admissible controls $u:[0,T]\to U$, generating flows $\Phi_t^{u(\cdot)}:\mathcal{P}(M)\to\mathcal{P}(M)$ on the space of measures.

Problem. Develop a mathematically substantive control theory for such controlled MDEs at the level of the induced flows $\Phi_t^{u(\cdot)}$ on $\mathcal{P}(M)$ (rather than at the level of individual solution curves), using geometric control techniques. Specifically:

(a) Define suitable notions of accessibility, controllability, and reachable sets for the semigroup of flows generated by a family of PVFs, in a setting where only an abelian monoid (and not a Lie algebra) structure is available.

(b) Establish analogues of the Chow–Rashevskii / orbit theorems and Krener-type accessibility results characterizing the reachable set $\mathcal{R}_T(\mu_0)=\{\Phi_T^{u(\cdot)}\mu_0 : u(\cdot)\text{ admissible}\}$ in terms of intrinsic geometric invariants of the family $\{V_u\}_{u\in U}$.

(c) Identify sufficient conditions on the family $\{V_u\}$ under which the flow-level control system is (approximately) controllable on $\mathcal{P}(M)$, and exhibit nontrivial examples in which these conditions can be verified.
artifact.category_tag: measure differential equations and geometric control
artifact.status_search_result: A literature check on measure differential equations driven by probability vector fields shows that the framework is well established (Piccoli and collaborators), but no published work appears to develop a flow-level geometric control theory replacing the missing Lie-algebra structure with an abelian monoid structure on PVFs. The question is posed as a research direction and no general controllability/accessibility results in this setting were located.

status_evidence.title: Measure Differential Equations
status_evidence.snippet: MDEs correspond to probability vector fields mapping measures on a Euclidean space to measures on its tangent bundle.
status_evidence.claim: Defines the MDE / PVF framework underlying the question.

status_evidence.title: Measure dynamics with Probability Vector Fields and sources
status_evidence.snippet: Probability vector fields with sources, generalizing transport and diffusion of measures.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms ongoing development of MDE theory; no flow-level geometric control results are reported.
